courses.name: Special Studies in Baroque Music
courses.title: MUHL 585 - Special Studies in Baroque Music

sections.notes: Description: This course focuses on music and culture in Florence in the time of Medici rule. It begins in Medieval Florence in the time of the Black Death and Florentine composer Francesco Landini and continues with famous 15th c. foreigners invited to compose for the Medici family, such as G. Dufay and Heinrich Isaac. The course will focus on the far-reaching influence of Savonarola on Florentine music, the creation of the Frottola, the Madrigal and 16th century Intermedi, to Medici support of the creation of early Opera. We will discuss the influence of Medici women on music and culture in the 17th c. and include female artists such as composer Francesca Caccini and painter Artemesia Gentileschi. The course concludes with the Medici familys demise in the 1700s.

courses.title: MUHL 586 - Special Studies in the Music of the Classical Period, 1730-1800

sections.notes: Description: The course will focus on various aspects of Mozart's life and compositions, with close examination of specific works in various genres. Students will integrate readings on biography and cultural history with analytical study of specific pieces for class presentation and written assignments.

courses.name: Special Studies in Music Since 1900
courses.title: MUHL 588 - Special Studies in Music Since 1900

sections.notes: Description: This class will focus on three great generations of music and rhetorical theory from the period Orlando Lassus and Claudio Monteverdi, Heinrich Sch|tz and his students, from the time Johann Sebastian Bach and contemporaries. We will also follow this tradition of music rhetoric into the Classical Era, and touch on its "pre-history" in medieval music. Because understanding traditions of musical and rhetorical can have a major impact on how we approach performance of music from any generation, students can focus their research and analysis on links between music and meaning from periods and repertories of their choice.
